answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to prove control of a unique physical quill (one-time-use signed stylus) that etches a commitment into a shared prism (optical multi-path verifier) before accessing the jetty (entry dock). Attackers must acquire and destroy a new quill per fake identity%2C costing real manufacturing and logistics resources that scale linearly with Sybil count%2C while honest agents reuse their single quill indefinitely.
